timeframes.label: This Week
timeframes.simpleExplanation: Do these right now — they're the most urgent and set everything else in motion.

timeframes.label: This Month
timeframes.simpleExplanation: These are your big moves for the month. Each one gets you closer to having a real, official nonprofit.

timeframes.label: Next 3 Months
timeframes.simpleExplanation: These are the medium-term goals. By the time you finish these, your nonprofit will be running programs and applying for serious funding.

timeframes.label: 6+ Months
timeframes.simpleExplanation: These are the bigger vision items. They'll happen naturally as Phase 1 gets rolling.

todos.title: Search for Nonprofit Name
todos.description: Go to businessfilings.sc.gov and search for name availability. Try: Southern AI Literacy Initiative, Palmetto AI Project, Roots & Algorithms, The Digital Harvest Initiative.

subtasks.title: Brainstorm 5 name options
Search each on SC business filings
Check domain availability for top 3 names
Reserve top choice name ($10)

todos.title: Identify 2-3 Potential Board Members
todos.description: Reach out informally to people who can fill three roles: nonprofit governance experience, tech/AI knowledge, and deep community ties. You don't need all three in one person — spread it across your board.

subtasks.title: List 6-8 candidates from your network
Identify which gap each candidate fills
Send casual 'I'm building something' message to top 3

todos.title: Draft 1-Page Concept Overview
todos.description: Write a one-pager that you can hand to potential partners, board members, and funders. Include: mission statement, the 3-phase vision, what communities you serve, and what you're looking for (partners, board members, early supporters).

subtasks.title: Write mission statement (1-2 sentences)
Summarize 3-phase vision in plain language
Describe target communities and problem being solved
Add a clear call to action (what you need)
Design a clean, shareable PDF version

todos.title: Reach Out to Kim Bowman (SCRIN)
todos.description: Kim Bowman at the SC Rural Innovation Network is the most important early connection you can make. SCRIN already has trust in rural communities across SC — a relationship here opens doors to pilot sites, credibility, and rural-specific funding. Find her on LinkedIn or through the SC Office of Rural Health.

subtasks.title: Find Kim Bowman on LinkedIn or SCRIN website
Draft personalized intro message
Send message or email

todos.title: Contact UofSC Office of Innovation
todos.description: Leverage your alumni status to open doors at USC. The Office of Innovation connects alumni entrepreneurs with university resources, incubator space, and faculty experts. Ask specifically about the Technology Incubator and any AI or civic tech programs.

subtasks.title: Find contact info for UofSC Office of Innovation
Draft email mentioning alumni status and nonprofit focus
Ask about incubator access and faculty partnerships

todos.title: Visit USC/Columbia Technology Incubator
todos.description: Go see the space in person. Walking in as an alumni founder creates a very different impression than an email. Meet current founders in the building, get a feel for the ecosystem, and ask about what it takes to get space there.

subtasks.title: Look up address and visiting hours
Prepare 60-second intro of your project
Visit, introduce yourself, and take notes on what you learn

todos.title: Reach Out to Rep. Jeff Bradley's Office
todos.description: Rep. Jeff Bradley (SC House) represents Beaufort and is reachable as a constituent. Ask for a brief constituent meeting or send an intro email about your AI literacy work. Elected officials love being early supporters of community-benefit tech initiatives — this could lead to introductions, advocacy, and eventual public funding.

subtasks.title: Find contact info for Rep. Bradley's district office
Draft constituent intro email about the project
Send email and request a brief meeting

todos.title: File Articles of Incorporation
todos.description: Go to sos.sc.gov and file your Articles of Incorporation online. This is the document that officially creates your nonprofit as a legal entity in South Carolina. Filing fee is $32.50. You'll need your name (once confirmed available), registered agent, and board member info.

subtasks.title: Confirm nonprofit name is available and reserved
Identify registered agent (can be yourself)
Gather board member names and addresses
Complete and submit Articles of Incorporation at sos.sc.gov ($32.50)
Save confirmation and certificate of incorporation

todos.title: Get EIN from IRS
todos.description: Apply for your Employer Identification Number (EIN) at IRS.gov. It's free and takes about 10 minutes online. You'll receive it instantly. You cannot open a bank account, apply for tax exemption, or accept most grants without an EIN.

subtasks.title: Have Articles of Incorporation ready before applying
Go to IRS.gov EIN online application
Complete application (select 'Other nonprofit/tax-exempt organizations')
Save EIN confirmation letter (CP 575)

todos.title: Hold Organizational Board Meeting
todos.description: Once you have your board members identified, hold your first official meeting. Virtual is fine. You need to formally approve your bylaws, elect officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer at minimum), and document it in meeting minutes. This is a legal requirement before filing for 501(c)(3) status.

subtasks.title: Finalize board member commitments
Draft or adapt nonprofit bylaws template
Schedule meeting (Zoom or in-person)
Conduct meeting: approve bylaws, elect officers
Document meeting minutes and have board sign

todos.title: File Form 1023-EZ for 501(c)(3) Status
todos.description: This is the most consequential filing you'll make. Form 1023-EZ is the streamlined version of the federal tax-exempt application, available for organizations expecting under $50K/year in revenue initially. Filing fee is $275. Once approved, donations to your organization are tax-deductible and you can apply for foundation and government grants. File at pay.gov.

subtasks.title: Confirm eligibility for 1023-EZ (under $50K projected revenue)
Gather required docs: EIN, Articles, Bylaws, board member info
Complete Form 1023-EZ at pay.gov
Pay $275 filing fee
Save IRS determination letter when received (typically 2-4 weeks)

todos.title: Set Up Website and Social Channels
todos.description: Use your design and dev skills here — this is your chance to make the organization look credible from day one. A clean website with your mission, team, and a way to contact you does more than any pitch deck. Also set up LinkedIn (most important for this work), Twitter/X, and Instagram.

subtasks.title: Register domain name
Build or deploy basic website (mission, team, contact)
Create LinkedIn organization page
Create Instagram and Twitter/X accounts
Post first piece of content on each platform

todos.title: Begin Drafting First Grant Application
todos.description: Target the OpenAI People-First AI Fund as your first major grant attempt. Start drafting even before you have your 501(c)(3) determination — the writing process will sharpen your mission and make every future application faster. Focus on your story, the problem in rural SC, and your specific approach.

subtasks.title: Research OpenAI People-First AI Fund eligibility and requirements
Outline grant narrative (problem, solution, approach, impact)
Draft budget for proposed program activities
Write first full draft of application

todos.title: Pilot First AI Literacy Workshop
todos.description: Partner with SCRIN or a local library to run your first real workshop. Keep it small — 10 to 20 people is a great first run. Focus on something practical: what AI tools exist, how to use them safely, what they mean for jobs in their community. Document everything for grant applications.

subtasks.title: Confirm venue partner (SCRIN, library, or community center)
Design workshop curriculum (2-3 hours, hands-on)
Promote event to target community
Run workshop
Collect participant feedback forms
Write post-event summary with photos and metrics

todos.title: Apply for USDA Rural Business Development Grant
todos.description: The USDA Rural Business Development Grant (RBDG) funds technical assistance and training projects that benefit rural small businesses and communities. Grants range from $10K to $500K. This is a natural fit for an AI literacy and workforce development program in rural SC.

subtasks.title: Research current USDA RBDG application window at rd.usda.gov
Contact local USDA Rural Development office in SC
Prepare application with program narrative and budget
Submit application before deadline

todos.title: Apply for Google for Nonprofits
todos.description: Google for Nonprofits gives qualified 501(c)(3) organizations free Google Workspace (email, Drive, Meet) and up to $10,000/month in free Google Ads through the Ad Grants program. You need your IRS determination letter first. Apply at google.com/nonprofits.

subtasks.title: Wait for IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
Register with TechSoup (required intermediary)
Apply at google.com/nonprofits
Set up Google Workspace for organization
Activate and configure Google Ad Grants account

todos.title: Build Relationships with aiEDU, CORI, and 4-H
todos.description: These three organizations are natural curriculum and partnership allies. aiEDU builds AI literacy curriculum you can use or adapt. CORI (Center on Rural Innovation) focuses on rural tech ecosystems. 4-H has deep rural community trust and infrastructure across SC. Start with warm intro messages to each.

subtasks.title: Research each org's mission, current programs, and key contacts
Send intro email to aiEDU
Send intro email to CORI
Contact SC 4-H state office about collaboration
Schedule follow-up calls with interested contacts

todos.title: Document Everything
todos.description: Start building your evidence base now. Every workshop, every meeting, every email from a community member about impact — save it. Photos, testimonials, attendance numbers, pre/post surveys. This is what turns a grant application from 'promising idea' to 'proven approach.' Create a simple shared folder system.

subtasks.title: Create Google Drive folder structure for program documentation
Design a simple participant feedback form
Take photos at every event (with permission)
Collect 3-5 written testimonials after first workshop
Write a monthly impact summary starting Month 1

todos.title: Apply for OpenAI People-First AI Fund
todos.description: The OpenAI People-First AI Fund is one of the most relevant grants for this work — it specifically supports organizations helping communities navigate AI's impact on work and society. Monitor openai.com/foundation for the next application window. By this point you'll have your 501(c)(3) status and a pilot workshop to point to.

subtasks.title: Monitor openai.com/foundation for next application window
Refine grant narrative using pilot workshop data
Submit application with full documentation package

todos.title: Establish Corporate Sponsorships
todos.description: Tech companies increasingly need ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) and CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) visibility. An AI literacy nonprofit in a rural Southern state is a compelling, differentiated story for a tech company's impact report. Target Salesforce, Microsoft, IBM, and regional tech employers in SC.

subtasks.title: Build a corporate sponsorship deck (1-2 pages)
Create tiered sponsorship levels with clear benefits
Identify and research 10 target companies
Make first outreach to 3-5 companies

todos.title: Design Incubator Curriculum
todos.description: Phase 2 is the AI-native business incubator for rural SC entrepreneurs. Start designing the curriculum: what does someone need to know to build a business using AI tools in 2026? Focus on practical tools (not theory), real business use cases, and the specific challenges of rural markets.

subtasks.title: Research existing business incubator curriculum models
Interview 5-10 rural entrepreneurs about their AI knowledge gaps
Draft 6-week curriculum outline
Test key modules in Phase 1 workshops

todos.title: Plan First Hackathon Event
todos.description: A community hackathon is a high-visibility event that attracts press, sponsors, and talent. Themed around 'AI solutions for rural SC problems' — farming, healthcare access, economic development. Plan for 50-100 participants, a day-long format, and small cash prizes funded by sponsors.

subtasks.title: Choose format, date, and venue
Recruit sponsors for prizes and catering
Build registration and marketing plan
Recruit judges and mentors

todos.title: Research SEC Requirements for Phase 3
todos.description: Phase 3 involves a community angel fund and potentially a hedge fund structure for AI-driven rural investment. Before you get there, you need to understand SEC regulations for investment vehicles, accredited investor rules, and how a nonprofit can legally operate alongside or spin off a for-profit investment entity. Get an attorney involved.

subtasks.title: Consult with a securities attorney about fund structures
Research accredited investor rules and Reg CF crowdfunding
Explore CDFIs (Community Development Financial Institutions) as a model
Draft a preliminary Phase 3 legal structure memo
